trigger: JN2 is down when the new writer (epoch 2) runs newEpoch and startLogSegment(4). JN2 restarts and receives journal() for segment 4 with epoch 2 while its lastWriterEpoch is still 1. Later JN0 is stopped.
reason: JN2 never opened segment 4, so it must not accept edits for it. If lastWriterEpoch matched, Journal.journal would still reject with 'Can't write, no segment open' (Journal.java:405-406). checkWriteRequest (Journal.java:517-520) is just the first of these equivalent guards. The client handles the failure as designed: IPCLoggerChannel.sendEdits marks the logger outOfSync with the log 'Will try to write to this JN again after the next log roll' (IPCLoggerChannel.java:363-369), and the JN rejoins at the next segment roll. A JN that misses part of a segment is excluded until the next roll by design. The reduced-redundancy window is the documented behaviour, and it heals on its own at the next roll.
